config.grain_rationale: Each row is one employment-services SITE (office/location) operated by a provider under a specific employment services contract (CONTRACT_NAME, e.g. DESA/DESB/EPS5). The business participant is the provider organisation named in SITE_NAME; the row describes that provider's site: address, state, postcode, website, email and phone contacts. DIS_SITE_CODE is the site identifier, not a business identifier, so it is not mapped to the entity.

record_id.rationale: DIS_SITE_CODE is not unique per record (489 distinct over 505 rows) because the same site appears once per contract code. No other column or combination is guaranteed unique, so a content hash over all mapped source fields is used for traceability.

fields.rationale: SITE_NAME holds the provider's operating/brand name (e.g. 'MAX Employment', 'Advanced Personnel Management', 'CoAct/Community Solutions', 'Job Centre Australia'). These are trading/display names, not evidenced registered legal names, so trading_name (not legal_name). Note the same provider appears under several variants (e.g. 'Advanced Personnel Management' vs '(APM)').
SITE_URL contains provider domains such as 'www.apm.net.au' or 'http://maxsolutions.com.au/'; present in 57.6% of rows.
Street address line(s) of the site, e.g. '2nd Floor 22 East Row', 'Shop 6 & 7 The HUB Wynyard Street'. Values are truncated at ~40 chars in the source.
Suburb/town of the site, e.g. 'CANBERRA', 'WOY WOY'; same value domain as LOCATION_NAME (412 distinct each).
Two/three letter AU state abbreviation (8 distinct values: NSW,VIC,QLD,SA,WA,TAS,NT,ACT).
4-digit AU postcodes; 13 of 505 are 3-digit (NT codes such as 822) which the postcode transform re-pads.

constants.rationale: Australian government register of Australian employment-services sites; all states are AU state codes and postcodes are AU format.

unmapped.reason: Short site code (e.g. A230, V352) with no checksum; not unique per record (same site repeats across contract codes). The record's own site ID, not a business identifier.
Employment-services contract type (DESB, DESA, EPS5, TTW5, RJCP...) describing the program under which the site is contracted, not an attribute of the business entity.
Duplicates SITE_LOCALITY_NAME (same 412 distinct value domain) - the site's town; already captured via address.locality.

Blank in 100% of discovery rows (wrapped second ESA code).
Blank in 100% of discovery rows (wrapped third ESA code).
13/1800 freecall number for the agent; phone is not an ontology target and conflicts with per-site numbers.

config.notes: No ABN/ACN/NZBN column exists in this extract (checksum-valid rates on numeric columns are ~0%), so no business identifier can be mapped. entity_type is left out because no column states a legal structure. SITE_NAME is used as trading_name, not legal_name, because values are brand names with inconsistent variants. discovery profiling covers a 505-row partition.

fields.reason: SITE_NAME holds operating/brand names (e.g. 'Vision Australia', 'Maxima Group Training'), which are display/trading names, not evidenced registered legal names. Correctly mapped to trading_name rather than legal_name. Note some are franchises ('Sarina Russo Job Access') but still operating names.
SITE_URL holds provider domain values; empty values correctly dropped. The website transform may or may not prepend scheme, but the semantic target (entity website) is correct.

SITE_ADDRESS_LN is the site's premises street address, which matches address.full semantically. However the dataset grain is 'establishment' and address.full is a single-field canonical address; without explicit signalling that this is a premises (not postal) address, downstream consumers may misinterpret. The rationale does not flag premises vs postal. Still, the actual street address values support ok; flagging doubtful only due to missing explicit premises designation.
Suburb/town of the site; matches locality. Upper-cased consistently. LOCATION_NAME duplicates this and is correctly left unmapped.
Two/three-letter AU state abbreviations (ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, VIC), all valid enum values. No guessing of unusual values observed.

AU 4-digit postcodes; NT 3-digit values (e.g. '850' -> '0850') are re-padded. The padding is a normalisation choice but produces a syntactically valid AU postcode for NT. Values matched the state (e.g. QLD 4625 for Gayndah is plausible).
Constant 'AU' is justified: all states are AU state codes and postcodes are AU format; no NZ/OTHER values present in heldout.

missed.reason: Not a website. However, many values are generic organisational addresses (e.g. 'jobfind_katherine@jobfindcentre.com.au'), which could be useful contact info but the ontology has no email target. Not a true match; noted only because it was deliberately excluded — do not force.
No phone target in ontology; correctly left unmapped.

critic.summary: Mapping is largely sound. SITE_NAME is correctly treated as trading_name (not legal_name), addresses and state/postcode are correctly typed, and website values are genuine provider domains. The only notable ambiguity is address.full being sourced from a site premises street line without an explicit premises-vs-postal designation; it is semantically correct but should be flagged as a premises address. No business identifiers (ABN/ACN) or entity_type columns exist in the source, so their absence is expected and not a missed mapping. No significant source column that clearly matches an ontology target was left unmapped.

config.notes: No ABN/ACN/NZBN column exists in this extract (checksum-valid rates on numeric columns are ~0%), so no business identifier can be mapped. entity_type is left out because no column states a legal structure. SITE_NAME is trading_name, not legal_name: values are brand names with inconsistent variants. address.full is explicitly the PREMISES (street) address of the site, not a postal address. Held-out fixes: placeholder 'TBA' now nulled in address fields and SITE_NAME; SITE_URL gated by a domain-shaped regex so junk values (bare phone numbers, 'TTY: ...') are dropped instead of erroring.

fields.reason: SITE_NAME holds provider operating/brand names ('Vision Australia', 'Sarina Russo Job Access', 'OCTEC Limited'); treating them as trading/display names rather than legal names is the conservative and correct choice. 'OCTEC Limited' could be a legal name but not evidenced as registered, so trading_name is safe.

Values are genuine provider domains (www.visionaustralia.org.au, http://www.novaemployment.com.au). The domain-shaped regex plus null_if correctly drops junk phone-like values observed in discovery while preserving real URLs. Output format preserves scheme/case where present; acceptable.

SITE_ADDRESS_LN is premises street address (unit/level + street number + street name), matching address.full. The rationale explicitly notes it is premises, not postal. No suite/level subfields exist in the ontology so no important information is being misassigned.
Suburb/town of site; consistent with SITE_LOCALITY_NAME values (CANBERRA, GAYNDAH, HILLCREST). Upper-casing is a normalisation, acceptable.
Two/three-letter AU state codes map cleanly to AU enum via state op. ACT/NSW/QLD/VIC/SA all valid.
4-digit AU postcodes; NT 3-digit '850' correctly zero-padded to '0850'. Reasonable normalisation for AU postcodes.
Constant 'AU' justified: Australian government register, AU states and postcodes throughout the held-out sample.

missed.reason: Not appropriate: CONTRACT_NAME (DESB/DESA/EPS5/TTW5/RJCP/HLS5/SPP5/NEI5) is an employment-services programme code, not ANZSIC. Correctly left unmapped; no ANZSIC source present. Not a genuine miss.
No — emails are not websites; some are personal staff addresses. Correctly excluded; ontology has no email target.
Not applicable: ontology has no geo target and geocoordinates are not an address string. Correctly unmapped.
Duplicate of SITE_LOCALITY_NAME; already captured. Correctly unmapped to avoid duplicate observations.

critic.summary: All mapped fields are semantically correct for their canonical targets given the ontology. SITE_NAME is properly treated as trading_name (conservative, since legal names are not evidenced). Website regex correctly gates out junk phone-like values seen in discovery. Address fields map premises street address, locality, state, and AU postcode with correct zero-padding of NT 3-digit codes. The unmapped columns (DIS_SITE_CODE, CONTRACT_NAME, ESA codes, phones, LAT/LONG, email) are appropriately excluded because the ontology has no corresponding targets or they are duplicates/administrative codes, not business identifiers. No wrong enum guesses, no entity_type/legal_name/ABN fabrications were made. No genuine missed source columns.
